blocks.text: Genes from a wide range of organisms can be added to a plasmid and inserted into bacteria. Transgenic bacteria can synthesize large amounts of the proteins encoded by the inserted foreign genes. Different forms of transgenic bacteria are being used to;

items: Produce pharmaceutical products e.g., insulin (to treat diabetes), clotting factors (to treat haemophilia), hepatitis B vaccine (against hepatitis B), Covid-19 vaccine (against Corona), human growth hormone (to treat dwarfism), interferon (to treat some cancers), erythropoietin (to treat anaemia), and tissue plasminogen activator (which dissolves blood clots).
Produce many food products e.g., alpha-amylase (converts starch to simple sugars), chymosin (clots milk protein for cheese making), and pectin-esterase (improves fruit juice clarity).
Produce enzymes which degrade toxins to convert pollutants into a less toxic form.
Leach copper from ore, clean up mercury pollution and detect arsenic in drinking water.
